Linear regressions for titrations that exceeded 30 points (n>30). For titrations close to finishing, the endpoint can be determined via linear regression, with the intercept as the endpoint. Below are regressions for samples where n>30. The regressions were run with points where the current was less than 5uA. 

```{python}

#| echo: false
#| warning: false

##Estimation of endpoint via linear regression##
#For circumstances when n>30, titration times out
#Just do a linear regression with current on the x-axis and microliters of thio on the y-axis.  The y-intercept will be a close approximation of the endpoint. -C. Langdon

#import modules
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy as sp
from scipy import stats
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt 

#loop for multiple regressions--file names built on station and flask number, create lists of both
stn_list = ['stn names']

flsk_list = [1]


for i, j in zip(stn_list, flsk_list): 

  #define station and flask for automation
  stn = i
  flsk = j

  #file name
  trt_file = r"C:\Users\rc_local\Documents\A16S O2\Regression Files\A16S_{}_{}.csv".format(stn, flsk)

  #read in csv with
  df = pd.read_csv(trt_file)

  #print dataframe
  #print(df)

  #convert to numpy arrays 
  uL_thio = df['uL_thio'].to_numpy() 
  current = df['current'].to_numpy()

  #plot current and thio 
  fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize = (8,3), layout = 'constrained')
  ax1.scatter(current, uL_thio, color = "b", marker = "o", s = 30)

  #invert axis
  plt.xlim(max(current), min(current))
  plt.ylim(max(uL_thio), min(uL_thio))

  #label axis
  ax1.set_xlabel('current (uA)')
  ax1.set_ylabel('thio (uL)')
  title_str1 = 'Titration Plot'
  ax1.set_title(title_str1);


  #slice out current <5
  uL_thio_5 = uL_thio[current<5]
  current_5 = current[current<5]

  #linear regression via scipy

  slope, intercept, r, p, std_err = stats.linregress(current_5, uL_thio_5) 

  def myfunc(current_5):
    return slope * current_5 + intercept

  mymodel = list(map(myfunc, current_5))

  #plot titration

  ax2.scatter(current_5, uL_thio_5, color = "m", marker = "o")

  #invert axis
  plt.xlim(max(current_5), min(current_5))
  plt.ylim(max(uL_thio_5), min(uL_thio_5))

  #plot best fit line
  ax2.plot(current_5, mymodel, color = "g")

  #label axis
  ax2.set_xlabel('current (uA)')
  #ax2.set_ylabel('thio (uL)')

  int_str = 'y-intercept: {}'.format(round(intercept,2))
  title_str2 = 'Linear Regression (<5uA)'
  ax2.legend(title = int_str)
  ax2.set_title(title_str2);

  title_str = 'Station {} Flask {}'.format(stn, flsk)
  fig.suptitle(title_str);

  #calculate regression coefficients
  #run regression for current < 5

  #rename
  x = current_5
  y = uL_thio_5

  def estimate_coef(x, y):
    # number of observations/points
    n = np.size(x)

    # mean of x and y vector
    m_x = np.mean(x)
    m_y = np.mean(y)

    # calculating cross-deviation and deviation about x
    SS_xy = np.sum(y*x) - n*m_y*m_x
    SS_xx = np.sum(x*x) - n*m_x*m_x

    # calculating regression coefficients
    b_1 = SS_xy / SS_xx
    b_0 = m_y - b_1*m_x

    return (b_0, b_1)

  estimate_coef(x,y)
```
